p0765: How to spot a fake job offer – Workify
p0766: Most job scams follow the same pattern. These are the signs to watch for, and what to check before you pay anything or hand over your passport.
p0768: They ask you for money: a registration fee, a visa fee, a medical fee or a “deposit” to keep the job.
p0769: The pay is far above what similar jobs in that country offer.
p0770: There is no written contract, or they want you to sign a contract you cannot read.
p0771: Everything happens on WhatsApp or social media, with no company name, address or licence number.
p0772: They want your original passport, or tell you to travel on a tourist or visit visa and “change it later”.
p0773: They push you to decide today, or ask you to keep the offer secret from your family.
p0774: The company name, e-mail address or website is slightly different from the real employer's.
p0776: Find the agency's licence number and check it with the official office in your country.
p0777: Ask for the written offer and contract in a language you understand, and compare them with the job ad.
p0778: Check that your visa is a work visa for the same employer and the same job as in your contract.
p0779: Do not pay anyone to get the job. The ILO's fair recruitment principles say workers should not be charged recruitment fees or related costs.
p0780: If something feels wrong, ask in the Workify chat or report the job. We check every report.
p0782: Keep every receipt, message and bank transfer. Write down names, phone numbers and dates.
p0783: Report the agency to the labour or foreign employment office in your country, and report the job on Workify so we can stop it reaching other workers.

p0803: Working in Europe: permits explained – Workify
p0805: A verified employer or agency offers you a job and a contract.
p0806: The employer applies for permission to hire you. In many countries the labour office first checks the job and the pay.
p0807: You apply for a work visa (often a national “D” visa) at the country's embassy or visa centre, with the documents the employer sends you.
p0808: After you arrive, you register your address and receive a residence permit card.
p0809: At first your permit is usually tied to your employer. Ask what happens if you want to change jobs.
p0811: Pay in Europe is usually stated gross, before tax and social insurance. Ask how much you receive net.
p0812: You pay for your own housing unless the contract says otherwise. Ask what the rent is and whether it is taken from your pay.
p0813: Some jobs need your qualification recognised, for example in care or electrical work. This can take months.
p0814: Visa and permit processing can take weeks or months. Do not leave your current job before your visa is issued.
p0815: The EU Immigration Portal explains the rules of each EU country in many languages.
p0816: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania and Kosovo are not in the EU and have their own work permits. A permit there does not let you work in EU countries.
p0817: Serbia has issued a single permit for residence and work since 2024, applied for online. Official information is on the Welcome to Serbia portal.

p1000: An agency sees your profile when you apply to it, and only the documents you choose for that application. Access ends when the application is withdrawn or closed. If you switch on “Show my profile to verified agencies”, verified agencies also see your first name and surname initial, trade, skills, experience, languages, countries, start date and expected pay – never your documents, phone number or e-mail. Reviews you write are public with your first name, surname initial and country. Our verification team sees company documents, not workers' documents.
p1002: As long as your account exists. When you delete your account, we delete your profile, documents, applications and messages. Security records are kept for a limited time.
p1004: You can download your data and delete your account at any time in Settings. You can also ask us to correct your data or limit its use, and you can complain to your data protection authority.
p1005: Documents are stored privately and opened only after an access check. Every time an agency opens a document, it is recorded.
p1007: We use one cookie that keeps you logged in and protects forms. It is necessary for the service, so we do not ask for consent. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

p1032: The rules every agency and employer accepts before publishing on Workify.
p1035: These terms apply to recruitment agencies and employers (“companies”) that use Workify. The person who registers confirms that they may act for the company.
p1036: Companies must not charge workers any fee or cost for recruitment – not for the job, the interview, the contract, the visa, the work permit, the ticket or the medical check – directly, through deductions from wages or through others. A breach closes the account at once.
p1038: Companies send their company registration and, for agencies, their recruitment licence. Workify checks them before the first job is published and may ask for them again at any time. Invalid documents close the account.
p1040: Every ad shows the real pay and says whether it is net or gross, the housing and its cost, and what the employer pays for. Timelines are estimates and must be realistic. Photos must show the real workplace and housing, without business names, signs or addresses.
p1042: Companies use workers' data and documents only for the application they were shared for, keep them safe and delete them when they are no longer needed. Contacting workers outside the platform to avoid these terms is not allowed.
p1044: Job ads cost €29 per published job per month; the agency subscription costs €149 per month. Prices are without VAT. Invoices are sent by e-mail and are due within 14 days by bank transfer. A featured ad costs €49 per 30 days and is marked as featured.
p1046: When a worker hired through Workify signs the contract, the company owes one month's pay of that job (the lower end of the advertised pay), in the job's currency, minus any loyalty discount. If the worker leaves within 5 days of starting, 70 % of the fee is refunded; within 20 days, 30 %. Instead of a refund, the company can choose one replacement without a new fee within 30 days. The company reports the departure in the application.
p1048: Workify may hide ads or suspend a company that breaks these terms, misleads workers or receives repeated justified reports. Fees already due stay due; fees for hires that do not happen are cancelled.
p1049: Questions about these terms or about invoices: support@example.com.
p1053: Workify connects workers with recruitment agencies and employers. Employment contracts are made directly between the worker and the employer or agency.
p1054: Workers never pay to get a job, for the visa or work permit process, or for a contract. Agencies and employers that charge workers, directly or through others, are removed.
p1056: In Europe, Western Balkans, workers can buy optional extras: priority in agencies' talent searches (€5 per 30 days) and a professional CV text (€9). They never influence a company's decision; applying stays free. The price is shown before ordering, the extra starts when the payment is confirmed, and an order can be cancelled by e-mail to support@example.com within 14 days if the extra has not started; the money is then refunded in full.
p1057: Agencies and employers must give correct company and licence details. We check them before jobs go live, but verification does not guarantee every job.
p1059: Every job must show the real pay, place and conditions. Misleading or fake posts are removed.
p1061: No harassment, no discrimination and no collecting data for other purposes. Report problems with the report button or at support@example.com.

p1065: Reviews must describe your own experience with an agency, without insults and without personal details of other people. We may hide reviews that break these rules. Agencies may invite workers only to real, open jobs, and an invitation never allows them to ask for money.
